The statement’s tone is risk-off: it acknowledges a sharp negative shock to activity and financial conditions while moving policy to the effective lower bound and launching large-scale asset purchases and liquidity support. The literature indicates that near the zero lower bound, nonstandard tools and credible commitments help stabilize demand (Svensson, 1997a; Svensson and Woodford, 1999). The Fed’s Treasury/MBS purchases and expanded repos are consistent with credit-channel/financial-accelerator insights that lowering external finance premia supports spending and investment (Bernanke-Gertler; Gertler and Gilchrist, 1994; Oliner and Rudebusch, 1996a). Dollar swap lines ease global funding strains, helping the flow of credit. Market-based inflation compensation fell while survey expectations were little changed, suggesting near-term disinflation pressures but relatively anchored long-run expectations—conditions under which forecast-targeting frameworks can aid stabilization. Despite a strong pre-shock labor market, the combined supply-and-demand nature of the pandemic shock and energy-sector stress implies recession risk that monetary policy can cushion but not fully offset at the ZLB. Overall, the extraordinary policy backstop modestly tempers, but does not erase, the negative outlook signaled in the text.
